clue.text: Cleared minimum payment we had sent round

indicators.note: the contracted 'we had' is sent all the way round the payment, enclosing it

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd
the smallest payment is one penny, 1p, read as the letters IP

explanation.surface: A household has only paid the bare minimum on a debt that they have just paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minimum payment' is the lowest coin, the penny, written 1p, and the figure one passes for the letter I; 'sent round' is a container signal, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a surface or a slate is to wipe it clean, so both verbs mean removing marks.

clue.text: Centre spread stays restricted

parts.note: the middle of the body, which spreads, is held in by stays, a corset; 'centre spread' reads like a magazine's middle pages

explanation.surface: A newspaper's middle pages are kept from wider circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are an old corset stiffened with whalebone.
explanation.definitionFit: A very narrow middle, achieved in fashion by tight corsetry that cinches a spreading body in.

clue.text: Showing lack of reverence for a poet's temple

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
fane is a poetic word for a temple

explanation.surface: Someone shows irreverence towards a temple that a poet loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent, blasphemous language or behaviour disrespects what is sacred.

clue.text: Throw overboard in Channel

definitions.meaning: a trench dug to carry water

explanation.definitionFit: To dump or abandon something, and a dug trench for water.

clue.text: For such exercises, most of the elastic is adjustable

indicators.note: something adjustable can be reset, so the letters are rearranged
most of a three-letter word is the word less its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym instructor notes that an elastic exercise band can be adjusted to suit the workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts THE to TH; with ELASTIC that gives THELASTIC, which 'is adjustable' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Running, jumping and throwing events form the sport whose collective name covers all such exercises.

clue.text: Ill-fated dog beset by wild cats

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the dog sits inside the cats
wild means out of control, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A doomed dog is surrounded by feral cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the cats, giving ACST, and 'beset by' means the dog is surrounded by that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under a curse means doomed, damned and unlucky.

clue.text: Shelter in middle of the leafy glade

indicators.note: the middle letter of the three-letter word is taken

parts.note: an arbour is a shady bower of trees or climbers

explanation.surface: Someone shelters in the centre of a leafy clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes H from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven for ships is a place of shelter, and as a verb it means to give refuge.

clue.text: Continually object over the French arch

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another is placed above it

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
les is French for 'the' (plural)
arch means sly, knowing

explanation.surface: Someone keeps objecting to a French triumphal arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts END above LES in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Without ever stopping, going on and on without a break.

clue.text: One who doesn't appreciate the resort of Tangier

indicators.note: a re-sort of the letters is a sorting again, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tourist is ungrateful for the holiday town of Tangier in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, sorting the letters of TANGIER again.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person shows no thanks for kindness received.

clue.text: Scarcely look at the time

parts.note: to scan is to look at closely
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone hardly glances at the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb in older English, it means barely or hardly.

clue.text: Lasting damage after imbibing drinks in fast vehicle

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the scar takes the drinks inside it

parts.note: a scar is permanent damage left on the skin
ports are fortified wines from Portugal

explanation.surface: A drink-driver crashes a fast car and is left permanently scarred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link; 'imbibing' is the container signal, the damage swallowing the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater built for speed and performance is a classic quick vehicle.

clue.text: Doctrine rejecting claim to be omnipotent

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the claim is read backwards

parts.note: someone claiming to be all-powerful says 'am God'

explanation.surface: A believer turns away from a teaching that seems to claim almighty power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns AM GOD back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of beliefs laid down as unquestionably true by an authority, such as a church, is its creed.

clue.text: Met experts providing this projection

parts.note: the Met is Britain's Met Office, whose meteorologists predict the coming conditions; 'projection' reads first as a map or cinema image

explanation.surface: Specialists at an institution present a projection of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK's national weather service; 'Met' looks like a past tense or the Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists publish a prediction of the coming days' rain, sun and wind, a projection of conditions.

clue.text: Batting out of turn is a bit off!

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is 'in'
ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
a turn is a stage act, as in a music-hall turn

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bats out of order is told that this is rather unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a short stage performance, as in variety theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slightly off is not quite correct, lacking precision.

clue.text: Diary is kept by a writer to express regret

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the writer holds the diary and is

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a log is a daily record or diary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer keeps a diary in which he says sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is fodder as well as part of the phrase 'is kept by'; the container signal is 'kept by' alone, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To say sorry is to show remorse for a wrong done.

clue.text: Particular relation

definitions.meaning: a particular point or detail, as in 'in every particular'
reference or connection, as in 'with regard to'

explanation.definitionFit: A detail or point is a particular ('in that particular'), and 'with regard to' means in relation to.

clue.text: Volunteers fencing in Japan with knight get humbled

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords
W is short for with, as in w/
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Volunteers fencing in Japan alongside a knight are brought low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like enclosing, but is the sport; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brought down a peg is to be made humble or deflated.

clue.text: They provide extra footage for cameramen

definitions.text: They provide extra footage for cameramen

parts.words: They provide extra footage for cameramen
parts.note: footage reads as filmed material, but here means feet: these camera stands have three legs

explanation.surface: Something gives camera crews additional film to work with.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged stands steady a camera, giving it extra feet to stand on.

clue.text: Arrangement of "The flowers that bloom in the spring", for example

definitions.text: Arrangement of "The flowers that bloom in the spring", for example

parts.words: Arrangement of "The flowers that bloom in the spring", for example
parts.note: the quotation looks like a song title being arranged musically (it is from The Mikado, set in Japan); the arrangement is of real flowers

explanation.surface: A musician arranges a Gilbert and Sullivan song.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is from The Mikado, set in Japan, which hints at the Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of flower arranging, which would arrange spring blooms.

clue.text: Ring person who's out

definitions.meaning: a small earring worn to keep a pierced ear open

explanation.definitionFit: A small earring keeps a piercing open, and someone asleep is out for the count.

clue.text: Moneylender's attempt to bolt

parts.note: a shy is a try or throw, as in coconut shy
a bolt is a lock on a door

explanation.surface: A moneylender tries to bolt the door against creditors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moneylender's' is 'Moneylender is'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The usurer in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice lends money at interest and demands his pound of flesh.

clue.text: One's standing up to play old instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is gives I is, written IS
to strum is to play a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician stands up to play an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns IS to SI; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Egyptian rattle with metal discs on a frame, used in worship.

clue.text: Discharge misdirected to foul water, initially

indicators.note: misdirected means sent the wrong way, so the letters are rearranged
initially means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A pipe wrongly sends its discharge into foul water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misdirected' turns TO FOUL into OUTFLO; 'initially' adds W from 'water'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid flowing out, like sewage released from a pipe, is a discharge.

clue.text: Don't go topless to remain cool

definitions.meaning: the literal sense: stay clothed on the upper body
the idiom: stay calm and do not lose one's temper

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay calm, while literally it means stay dressed above the waist.

clue.text: Recognises from a pronounced feature

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a person by a prominent facial feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like prominent, but signals a soundalike; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise something is to be familiar with it, to be acquainted with it.

clue.text: Read between the lines of finer composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A reader detects hidden meaning in a well-written essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges FINER; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce what is implied but not stated is to conclude from hints.

clue.text: Cook a pie containing this game

indicators.note: the words of the phrase contain the animal's name inside them

explanation.surface: A recipe tells you to bake a game pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means wild animals, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is any wild animal hunted; this striped African forest mammal is a relative of the giraffe.

clue.text: Disastrous for top oil shares listed here

indicators.note: disastrous suggests ruin, so the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Investors fear a collapse in leading oil company shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disastrous' rearranges FOR TOP OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor's holdings of shares and bonds are listed in a collection kept as a record.

clue.text: Entangled with curious kitchen instrument

parts.note: snared means caught in a trap or net
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange gadget in the kitchen gets tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'kitchen' is an orchestra's percussion section, not a room for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral players call the percussion section the kitchen, and this drum with wires across it belongs there.

clue.text: Fight with an ashplant?

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or fight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone picks a fight armed with an ash walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: An ashplant is usually an ash sapling cut as a stick; here it is a plant called an ash.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree also called mountain ash is an ash plant in a punning sense, hence the question mark.
